title: Fragile single-cone Dirac quantum walks in two dimensions
authors: C. W. J. Beenakker, J. Sánchez Férnan, J. Tworzydło
abstract: It is known that a one-dimensional (1D) quantum walk gives a local space-time discretization of the massless Dirac equation with a single quasi-energy cone (no fermion doubling at low energies), keeping the fundamental symmetries (chiral and time-reversal) of the continuum theory. We show that the analogous 2D construction is fundamentally more fragile. Local two-band quantum walks can have an unpaired Dirac cone, but the protecting symmetries then cease to be ordinary on-site symmetries: they become non-symmorphic, involving half-lattice translations, and are broken by generic spatial inhomogeneities. In particular, we demonstrate that the 2D Dirac quantum walk based on the Ho-Chalker network model can be gapped by potential scattering.
summary: The paper investigates the topological stability of 2D Dirac quantum walks compared to their 1D counterparts. Through symmetry analysis and advanced mathematical techniques involving Laurent polynomials, the authors prove that local 2D constructions cannot sustain an unpaired zero-energy Dirac cone because locality forces a specific parity ($P=+1$), leading to inevitable gap opening under realistic disorder or potential scattering.
main_problem: The core problem is determining if a two-dimensional (2D) Dirac quantum walk maintains topological protection against disorder, contrasting it with the known robustness in continuum systems.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that for local 2D quantum walks, the protecting symmetries required to maintain an unpaired zero-energy Dirac cone are incompatible with locality constraints, leading to gap opening under potential scattering or disorder.
method: The analysis combines symmetry arguments (chiral and time-reversal) with rigorous algebraic topology applied to the Floquet operator's Laurent polynomial representation on the torus.
model_or_system: The system is a local two-band quantum walk modeled by a unitary Floquet operator acting on position and spin in 2D space-time. It aims to mimic massless Dirac fermions, contrasting with the known robust 1D case.
key_observables: Quasi-energy dispersion relation $\epsilon(\mathbf{k})$, gap opening magnitude ($\Delta$), and topological invariants like parity $P$.
important_parameters: Potential scattering strength ($V$), momentum transfer vectors ($Q$), and the dimensionality (2D vs 1D).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a local, two-band spin-1/2 implementation of the quantum walk. The argument relies heavily on the algebraic characterization of locality via Laurent polynomials.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate momentum dependence of energy bands ($\epsilon(\mathbf{k})$), showing gap opening due to potentials ($V$ or $M$) in both the Ho-Chalker and squared QW models.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from comparing 1D vs 2D robustness, through specific model tests (Palindromic, Squared, Ho-Chalker), culminating in rigorous mathematical proofs using symmetry constraints and Laurent polynomials to show that locality forces $P=+1$, thus forbidding the unpaired cone.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical constraint on realizing topological edge/surface states using discrete quantum walks, showing that simple lattice discretizations fail where continuum models succeed, which is crucial for designing solid-state simulators or photonic analogs.
